question: The furnished products.aspose.org page for pdf/net states the library 'exposes 805 classes'. Our own extraction (TC-011, upstream commit b717287) found 899 TYPES. In the 300-type reduced fixture the kind split is 215 class_declaration / 81 enum / 3 interface / 1 struct, so 805 classes out of 899 types is not obviously reconcilable - extrapolating the sample gives roughly 644 classes, and the mission plan's own independent figure is 863. Three sources, three numbers, none currently cross-checked.
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: ingest the page, but the 805-classes sentence is marked unverified and must not be served as a citable fact until it is cross-checked against a full (non-reduced) extraction.
rationale: This is exactly the defect class the mission plan exists to prevent - a furnished page asserting a precise number that the deterministic tier does not corroborate. It cannot be resolved now because TC-011 deliberately committed a 300-type REDUCED fixture, so we cannot count classes across the full surface. TC-014 is the card that builds citation verification against raw knowledge; it is the right place to settle this. Blocking work now would stall the queue over a question that a later card is designed to answer.

question: search_docs doc content is sourced from repository-presenter's local sealed candidates rather than a live upstream README fetch, because repository-presenter cannot yet push to upstream repos and there is no tag or Co-Authored-By trailer to verify a live README's provenance. When should this switch to a live upstream fetch?
provisional_decision: Read repository-presenter's own local sealed candidate store (candidates/<org>__<repo>/CURRENT -> README.md) for now. Switch TC-119's source back to a live raw.githubusercontent.com fetch (this card's original, superseded design) once BOTH: (1) repository-presenter can push README changes to the real upstream repos, and (2) the resulting live commit/README carries an identifying tag or a Co-Authored-By: Repository Presenter <...>-style trailer marking its origin, so the switch itself is verifiable rather than assumed.
rationale: repository-presenter's own README documents real grounding/validation discipline (facts from the repo's own source/tests/examples, independent non-authoring review, proven reproducibility) that materially exceeds aspose.org's unreviewed pages - but its own project status confirms it does not yet open PRs against target repos, so a live upstream README's provenance cannot yet be machine-verified. The local sealed candidate is the strongest currently-verifiable source.

question: pdf/typescript has no sealed repository-presenter candidate yet (confirmed 2026-09-28: only an unsealed runs/clones/ checkout and a runs/transactions/<rev>/source/ snapshot exist under repository-presenter, no candidates/aspose-pdf-foss__Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-TypeScript/CURRENT). TC-119 therefore excludes it and leaves its furnished fixture on the old aspose.org-copied content. When should pdf/typescript's doc content be regenerated?
provisional_decision: Leave pdf/typescript's tests/fixtures/furnished/pdf_typescript/pages/_index.md unchanged by TC-119. Regenerate it the same way as the other 5 pilots (via a small follow-up card reusing TC-119's sealed_candidate_doc_fields) as soon as candidates/aspose-pdf-foss__Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-TypeScript/CURRENT exists in repository-presenter's own store.
rationale: Do not work around the gap by fetching pdf/typescript's live upstream README instead - that would reintroduce the unverifiable-provenance problem OQ-002 exists to avoid for the other 5 pilots, and do not fabricate sealed-candidate-shaped content that does not exist. An honest, tracked gap for one pilot is preferable to a silently inconsistent pipeline.

question: foss_mcp.normalization.document_schema.to_dict/from_dict (NormalizedDocument <-> JSON-able dict round-trip, schema_version-tagged) have zero production callers - infra/build_chunks.py builds a NormalizedDocument and immediately chunks it in-memory, never persisting/reloading it independently. The shape (explicit schema_version, nested Provenance/ValidationResult reconstruction) strongly suggests an intentional future document-level persistence/cache layer rather than leftover cruft, but no current card specifies one. Wire (build that persistence layer), or delete as premature API?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: leave to_dict/from_dict in place, unwired, exactly as-is. Do not delete (deleting a deliberately-shaped, round-trip-tested serialization API on code-level suspicion alone risks destroying a real future requirement for no measured benefit) and do not speculatively build a persistence layer with no consumer or requirement naming it (would violate this project's own no-speculative-abstraction discipline). Revisit when either (a) a future card needs document-level caching/persistence and can name a real consumer, or (b) a future unwired-symbol audit round has no remaining evidence of planned use, at which point delete.
rationale: Unlike with_validation (citation.py's validate_chunk already duplicates its exact logic inline - clear evidence of supersession, resolved by wiring without this open question) or build_manifest (a live production duplicate-construction site exists to wire into), to_dict/from_dict have no adjacent code either consuming them or duplicating their logic - there is no code-level signal pointing to wire vs delete, only a plausible but unconfirmed guess about future intent. Per AGENTS.md, a question the loop cannot answer from the evidence becomes a recorded provisional decision, not a stall.

question: The product-reference fetch (infra/fetch_product_reference.py via src/foss_mcp/extraction/manifest_reader.fetch_manifest_file) calls the unauthenticated GitHub Contents API, 60 requests per hour per IP. In the 2026-10-05 fourteen-pilot live run, cells-rust, slides-java and cells-go ingestion Jobs failed three times each with HTTP 403 rate limit exceeded, and because the fetch runs after publish and a failed Job blocks the serving init container, their serving pods never started. Should the fetch accept a token and should a rate-limited fetch stop blocking serving?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: leave the fetch unauthenticated for the POC and retry the rate-limited pilots after the hourly reset (verified: quota 30 of 60 remaining at 00:32, reset 01:21). Before any real deployment, add an optional GITHUB_TOKEN header read from a Kubernetes secret the owner provisions, and make a 403 or 429 retry with backoff and Retry-After instead of failing the Job. A credential is an owner item.
rationale: The failure is an environment quota, not a code defect, so it must not be hidden by weakening a check. It is still a real production fragility: a transient 403 permanently blocks a pilot unless the Job is rerun by hand. The token itself is an owner-only credential, so it cannot be done by the loop.

question: The cells/cpp and pdf/cpp pilots serve symbols but no documentation, because infra/build_chunks.py has no cpp entry in _PLATFORM_DISPATCH, so a furnished page cannot be ingested for C++ without a C++ example verifier. The verifier in src/foss_mcp/indexing/example_verifier.py is MSVC-only and cells-specific. When is the Linux g++/CMake verify path built so C++ documentation and verified examples are ingested?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: the POC proves C++ on the checks that apply (symbols, lookup, members, product reference, freshness, honest miss, isolation) and records search_docs and verified examples as not applicable for the two C++ pilots. Build a prepare/verify pair for cpp that compiles in the Linux container (feasible: pdf/cpp built with g++ 14 and CMake 3.31, recorded 2026-10-04), add the cpp entry to _PLATFORM_DISPATCH, then wire furnishedPage for cells/cpp and pdf/cpp.
rationale: Presenting a C++ pilot as documentation-complete without a verifier would claim verified examples that were never compiled. The gap is real, large, and independent of the MCP serving path, so it is tracked and not hidden.

question: The Linux C++ verifier (prepare_cpp_library_linux / verify_cpp_example_linux, TC-222) has never executed. Its one live test is deselected here, and this Windows host has no Linux g++ on PATH. Has the real pinned pdf/cpp library built and a real example verified inside the Linux ingestion image?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: the offline tests with subprocess mocked, the dispatch wiring and the negative control prove the code paths; the live proof is a G3 requirement. Run the live test in the Linux ingestion image (FOSS_MCP_NETWORK_TESTS=1, the image built by scripts/release/build_images.py) and record its result before G3 exit.
rationale: A passing offline suite does not prove a compiler path works on real source. Claiming verified C++ examples without that run would repeat the integration-liveness failure AGENTS.md describes, so the debt is recorded and gates G3.

question: The Linux C++ build needs network at build time: cmake configure downloads googletest from github.com (FetchContent) and the pinned library is fetched with git. Apt packages g++ and cmake are not pinned by exact version in Dockerfile.ingestion, and toolchain.lock.json has no row for them. Is this acceptable residual risk?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: keep the floating apt pins, following the file's existing rule for openjdk and maven, and record the exact versions in the Dockerfile comment (g++ 4:14.2.0-1, cmake 3.31.6-2). Add lock rows and an offline build path (a vendored googletest or a build-time network allowance) under a governed card before any production deployment.
rationale: The configure step cannot run without GitHub, the same origin as the pinned fetch the pipeline already needs. Exact apt pins would break on the next trixie update. Both are residual risks, recorded here rather than hidden.
